exposure: neuraxial analgesia techniques (epidural, dural puncture epidural (DPE), combined spinal-epidural (CSE))
cohort: The study included 10,971 patients who received neuraxial analgesia for labor and delivery pain management at a single maternity hospital in Dallas, Texas, comparing those delivered in 2019 to 2020 and those with and without SARS-CoV-2.
finding: While overall neuraxial techniques and complications did not change from 2019 to 2020, there was a significant increase in dural puncture epidural (DPE) use relative to epidurals in SARS-CoV-2-positive patients compared to SARS-CoV-2-negative patients in 2020, without affecting complication rates.
